# forgejo_team_repository (Resource)

Assigns one repository to an organization team. Permissions remain managed by `forgejo_team`.

The team and repository must belong to the same organization. Teams with
`includes_all_repositories = true` already have access and cannot be used to create
or import an individual assignment. Refreshing an existing assignment does not change
that setting. Destroy removes only the assignment, not the team or repository, and does
not revoke access granted by other teams, collaborators, or all-repositories access.

Import uses `org/team/repo` and only reads the existing configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    forgejo = {
      source = "svalabs/forgejo"
    }
  }
}

provider "forgejo" {
  host = "http://localhost:3000"
}

resource "forgejo_organization" "owner" {
  name = "test_org"
}

resource "forgejo_team" "developers" {
  name                      = "developers"
  organization              = forgejo_organization.owner.name
  includes_all_repositories = false
  units_map = {
    "repo.code" = "read"
  }
}

resource "forgejo_repository" "example" {
  owner   = forgejo_organization.owner.name
  name    = "example"
  private = true
}

resource "forgejo_team_repository" "assignment" {
  team_id       = forgejo_team.developers.id
  repository_id = forgejo_repository.example.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repository_id` (Number) Numeric identifier of the repository. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `team_id` (Number) Numeric identifier of the team. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the assignment in team_id/repository_id format.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Import using the organization, team, and repository names.
terraform import forgejo_team_repository.assignment test_org/developers/example
```
